newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: STATE BANK SALE MISUNDERSTOOD - PM.
newsitem.headline: STATE BANK SALE MISUNDERSTOOD - PM.

text.p: Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said on Thursday that the government's reasons for wanting to privatise the State Commercial Bank were "misunderstood."
"I think we'll sell State Commercial Bank, but the reason for selling this bank is misunderstood," Vagnorius told a news conference.
"I cannot agree with my opponents who say the government is selling this bank just to make a big profit," he said.

The government picked State Commercial Bank to be the first of three potential bank privatisations mainly because of its losses, but as of the July 1 deadline, the finance ministry had received no bids.
State Commercial Bank had a staggering 170 million litas loss last year and the state had to inject 165 million litas in fresh share capital after it ran into trouble last summer.
"We have to find a purchase price somehow to reduce losses," Vagnorius said.
The Agriculture Bank is expected to be privatised next.
Officials have said the possibility of privatising the other state-run bank, Lithuanian Savings Bank, depends on the success of the first two privatisations.
